LEARNING PATH · CLASS 45 · FAMILY & FRIENDS · AGES 4–5

Family & friends for kids — thirty-five printable family member cards to meet.

Thirty-five printable family and friends flashcards for ages four to five, all on this one page, in four shelves. Mum and dad, sisters and brothers, twins and babies, grandma and grandpa, aunties and uncles and cousins, the family gained at weddings, and the friends and neighbors all around: the people words kids reach for every day. Every card shows the word over its own smiling crowd of people, says who this person is in a family — plus one tiny way to make their day today — and downloads and prints straight from this page. Pick a card, print it, and the whole family album becomes a game.

Back to the Learning Path ↗
HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Every family is a team. Meet the whole roster.

Family words are usually the first words a child ever learns — mum, dad, baby — because people are what little kids study hardest. This class takes that study seriously: every card prints one word in big friendly letters over a whole crowd of the people it names, so a four-year-old sees that families come in every shape while the word sticks. You do not need a desk for this class. You need your family photo album, the people at your dinner table, and maybe a neighbor to wave at.

The shelves follow the family tree. The People in My House shelf starts with the ones you wake up next to — mum, dad, sisters, brothers, twins and babies. The Bigger Family shelf climbs the tree — grandmas, grandpas, aunties, uncles, cousins, nephews and nieces. The Married-in & Partners shelf celebrates the family gained at weddings — husbands, wives, partners and the in-laws. And the Friends & Neighbors shelf finishes with the people the family chooses — best friends, classmates, teachers and the team.

THE PEOPLE IN MY HOUSE SHELF · 10 CARDS

The people you wake up next to.

Printable family member flashcards for preschool and up: mum, dad, son, daughter, sister, brother, baby, twin, sibling and the word that holds them all — family. The first people words kids name every single day, one card each with a way to make their day. Every card carries its four pills — age, subject, grade level, skill — and its Download + Print buttons right under the picture, straight from this page.

THE BIGGER FAMILY SHELF · 10 CARDS

Grandmas, grandpas, aunties, uncles, cousins.

Family flashcards for ages 4–5 that grow the family tree: grandma and grandpa, aunt and uncle, cousin, nephew and niece, grandchild, parents and children — the people who fill the holidays and the photo albums. Every card carries its four pills — age, subject, grade level, skill — and its Download + Print buttons right under the picture, straight from this page.

THE MARRIED-IN & PARTNERS SHELF · 7 CARDS

Family gained at weddings.

Husband, wife, partner, girlfriend, boyfriend, brother-in-law and sister-in-law — the family members who arrive by wedding and by heart, each on its own printable card with one way to make them feel at home. Every card carries its four pills — age, subject, grade level, skill — and its Download + Print buttons right under the picture, straight from this page.

THE FRIENDS & NEIGHBORS SHELF · 8 CARDS

The people the family chooses.

Friend and best friend, neighbour, classmate, colleague, roommate, teacher and team — the friends flashcards for the people outside the house who make the day warmer, one printable card each. Every card carries its four pills — age, subject, grade level, skill — and its Download + Print buttons right under the picture, straight from this page.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where the family words grow up.

Feelings & Kindness in Class 38 · Ages 4–5 ↗Neighborhood walks in Class 33 · Ages 4–5 ↗Good habits in Class 32 · Ages 4–5 ↗The Learning Path ↗

Class 38 grows the feeling words — and feelings mostly happen around people: the sister who shares, the friend who helps, the grandma who listens. Class 33 walks the big neighborhood, where helpers like firefighters and doctors work beside the smaller helpers at home — the people on these cards. Class 32 practises the good habits, and this class names the people we practise them with. And when you want the next class, the Learning Path holds all forty-nine in order — and the whole deck prints again from the Family & Friends parents’ shelf.

Family is the first classroom. Every card here hands you a person to appreciate out loud — and your grown-up’s whole job is to say the word with you while you wave, hug, help or draw for them.
